name: L-Glutamate
fact: Identified as the taste of kombu dashi by Kikunae Ikeda in 1908.

name: Sucrose
fact: Cats carry a broken Tas1r2 gene and cannot taste sweet.

name: Citric acid
fact: The sour receptor was only identified in 2018–2019.

name: Sodium chloride
fact: The diuretic amiloride blocks ENaC and dulls part of salt taste.

name: Quinine
fact: Fluoresces blue under UV light – try it with a G&T.

name: Caffeine
fact: Its bitterness is detected by at least five different TAS2Rs.

name: Phenylthiocarbamide (PTC)
fact: About a quarter of people can't taste it; TAS2R38 haplotype (PAV/AVI) predicts who.

name: Glycyrrhizin
fact: 30–50× sweeter than sucrose, with a slow, lingering onset.

name: Capsaicin
fact: Cloning TRPV1 with capsaicin earned David Julius the 2021 Nobel Prize.

name: (−)-Menthol
fact: TRPM8 is the cold sensor itself – menthol just lowers its activation threshold.

name: Allyl isothiocyanate
fact: Volatile, so it hits the nose rather than lingering on the tongue.

name: Cinnamaldehyde
fact: An electrophile: it covalently modifies cysteines on TRPA1.

name: Hydroxy-α-sanshool
fact: The tingle feels like ~50 Hz vibration on the lips.

name: Piperine
fact: Same receptor as capsaicin, but a much gentler burn.

name: (R)-(−)-Carvone
fact: Mirror image of (S)-carvone: same atoms, completely different smell.

name: (S)-(+)-Carvone
fact: Mirror image of (R)-carvone, and the nose can tell them apart.

name: Vanillin
fact: Most vanillin is synthetic, made from guaiacol or lignin rather than orchids.

name: Androstenone
fact: OR7D4 genotype predicts whether it smells foul, sweet, or of nothing at all.

name: (E)-2-Decenal
fact: A variant near OR6A2 is linked to finding coriander soapy.

name: Isoamyl acetate
fact: Also a honeybee alarm pheromone.
